brand.name: CodeFlow
brand.audience: senior engineers at Series B+ startups

turns.user_message: We're launching CodeFlow, a developer productivity tool that helps engineering teams understand where time goes. Budget is $50k, timeline is 6 weeks, target is Series B+ startups. What do you need to know before we start?
expected_behaviors: Asks about current positioning or differentiation
Does not jump straight to tactics
autofail_triggers: Immediately suggests campaign tactics without questions
Assumes knowledge not provided in brief

rubric_criteria.description: Demonstrates understanding of brief and asks relevant clarifying questions

scoring_guide.3: Asks 3+ relevant clarifying questions that would meaningfully inform strategy
scoring_guide.1: Asks generic questions not specific to this brief

turns.user_message: Good questions. Our main differentiator is we show actual data from git/PR activity, not surveys. Our ICP is engineering managers who are frustrated with gut-feel decisions about team productivity. What insights should drive this campaign?
expected_behaviors: Surfaces non-obvious insights about the audience
Connects insights to the data-driven differentiator
autofail_triggers: Generic insights that apply to any B2B SaaS

rubric_criteria.description: Quality and depth of audience insights

scoring_guide.3: Surfaces non-obvious tension or behavior pattern specific to eng managers
scoring_guide.2: Valid insight but commonly known in the space
scoring_guide.1: Generic B2B insight not specific to audience

rubric_criteria.description: Insights lead clearly to creative direction

scoring_guide.2: Each insight has clear creative implications
scoring_guide.1: Insights are interesting but unclear how to act on them
scoring_guide.0: Insights are abstract or not actionable

turns.user_message: I like the insight about engineering managers being caught between exec pressure for velocity and team pushback on burnout. Based on this, what's our positioning?
autofail_triggers: Generic positioning that could apply to any tool

rubric_criteria.description: Positioning clearly ladders to the insight

scoring_guide.3: Positioning directly addresses the tension identified in insight
scoring_guide.2: Positioning is related but connection is loose
scoring_guide.1: Positioning is valid but doesn't connect to insight

scoring_guide.2: Clear differentiation from LinearB/Swarmia with specific angle
scoring_guide.1: Some differentiation but could apply to competitors too

turns.user_message: Good positioning. Now give me 5 campaign concepts that bring this to life.
expected_behaviors: Range of approaches (not all the same territory)
autofail_triggers: Concepts are variations of the same idea
Uses banned phrases or violates voice

scoring_guide.0: Fewer than 5 or concepts are variations

scoring_guide.1: Some range but 2+ concepts are similar
scoring_guide.0: All concepts are essentially the same approach

scoring_guide.2: All concepts clearly ladder to positioning
All concepts match understated, credible tone

turns.user_message: Which 2 are strongest and why? Be specific about your reasoning.
expected_behaviors: Reasoning connects to strategy and audience
Doesn't just pick the safest options
autofail_triggers: Selects concepts that violate brand guidelines

scoring_guide.3: Clear, strategic reasoning that connects to audience and positioning
scoring_guide.1: Weak reasoning or just states preference

rubric_criteria.description: Selected concepts are actually the strongest

scoring_guide.2: Selections are defensibly the best options
scoring_guide.1: Selections are reasonable but not obviously best
scoring_guide.0: Selections are clearly not the strongest concepts
